extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-26 reviewers (human reviewers, SPCs, ACs, program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewing submissions to the AAAI-26 Main Technical Track, covering what to check in the paper (technical contribution, evaluations, reproducibility, related work) and how to write constructive, depersonalized reviews. Includes procedures for interacting with AI-generated reviews and summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depersonalized professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, please do not use “I”, “you”, “the authors”, etc., in your reviews. Reviews should be depersonalized as much as possible. Use terms like “the paper”, “the work”, “the project”. The review should focus on the work and not the individuals (reviewers or authors). Avoid referring to yourself. If you must refer to yourself, it should be in the third person (e.g., “this reviewer”) and done sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal language and focus comments on the paper itself rather than on the authors. Use depersonalized nouns and limit first-person mentions to rare, third-person uses (e.g., 'this reviewer').

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful, constructive phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase your comments as would be appropriate if you were speaking respectfully to the authors face-to-face. Instead of “What is wrong with this paper?”, ask yourself “How could this paper be better?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques as suggestions for improvement rather than attacks; choose wording appropriate for a respectful conversation. Prefer constructive questions and concrete suggestions over blunt negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of suggested revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When suggesting revisions in the review, think about whether the revisions are reasonable in terms of time and resources — which of the recommendations are essential, and which are nice-to-have but optional?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate essential fixes (required for acceptance) from optional extensions; consider feasibility given typical authors' time and resources; label or explain major vs minor suggested changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity — the paper's story
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story of the paper clear? What is the problem that the paper aims to address?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the motivation, goal, and narrative arc are clearly presented. If unclear, point to specific sections or sentences that obscure the main story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of state-of-the-art limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the limitations in the state of the art that the paper addresses? Are the limitations clearly articulated, and reflective of the state of the art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the paper explains gaps in prior work and positions its contribution as addressing those gaps; call out missing citations or incorrect characterization of prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical claims support
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the empirical results really support the claims of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that experimental evidence matches the strength of claimed contributions; note overclaims and whether additional experiments or analyses are needed to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key novel technical contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the key novel technical contribution in the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and evaluate the central technical idea(s); assess novelty relative to prior work and whether the novelty is clearly articulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation: technical approach soundness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the technical approach sound and clearly described?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate formal correctness, clarity of derivations/algorithms, and whether the description is precise enough to understand the method. Highlight unclear steps or logical gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors, unstated assumptions, and missing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any errors, unstated assumptions, or missing details?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out concrete errors, questionable assumptions, or missing implementation/algorithmic details that prevent understanding or replication. Indicate severity and where fixes are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / sufficient detail for reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it expressed in sufficient detail to permit reproduction of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for availability of pseudo-code, hyperparameters, training details, dataset splits, seeds, and code or supplementary material; recommend what is needed to make experiments reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of limitations and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper clearly describe the limitations (in scope and generalizability) of its conclusions? (All work has limits, and it is vital to understand them.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit discussion of scope, failure modes, and contexts where results may not apply; encourage authors to acknowledge and quantify limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related work placement and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed contribution placed in the appropriate context of previous and related work, so as to allow a reader to draw connections between this work and others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness and accuracy of literature review, correct positioning relative to prior methods, and recommend missing citations or contrasts that clarify novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluations: appropriate baselines and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the empirical evaluation include appropriate baselines and comparisons to validate the proposed approach compared to the state of the art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure chosen baselines are strong and representative; suggest additional baselines if current ones are weak or missing; note when comparisons are unfair (e.g., missing tuning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluations: metrics reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the empirical evaluation report well-established and reasonable metrics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that metrics are standard, meaningful, and sufficient to support claims; recommend additional metrics if needed for a fuller picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluations: benchmarks and dataset choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the evaluation benchmarks and datasets appropriately chosen? Are there any better benchmarks or datasets that should have been used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dataset relevance, representativeness, and difficulty; recommend more appropriate or additional datasets/benchmarks where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error analysis in evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper include an analysis of errors made by the proposed approach?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for qualitative and quantitative error analyses that explain failure cases and guide future improvements; request such analysis if absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluations fully replicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the evaluations fully replicable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond describability, verify whether code, seeds, environment details, and data access permit independent replication; flag missing elements that block replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for improvement (research and presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: How could the research or the presentation of the paper be improved in light of the above?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, actionable recommendations tied to previous critique points; separate high-priority fixes from optional extensions and indicate expected effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding duplication of other reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers must not duplicate content from other reviews (neither the AI-generated nor human reviews), but are free to express their level of agreement with the points raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write independent assessments rather than copying wording; you may state agreement with others but add your own reasoning or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and flagging AI-generated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers will have the ability to make an official comment on the AI-generated review (distinct from the reviewer discussion), along with review ratings. These comments will only be visible to SPCs and higher. The Program Chairs, Workflow chairs, and Area Chairs will monitor comments made on AI-generated reviews to identify issues, and will take action as appropriate, such as re-generating the review, or excluding it entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the AI review contains errors or problematic content, use the official comment mechanism to flag it (visible to SPC+). Do not duplicate content from the AI review in your review, but you may update your review in light of clarified misunderstandings during rebuttal.
